newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall on finance, economic concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall on finance, economic concerns.

text.p: Thai stocks fell in early trade on Wednesday as worries surrounding the future of troubled Finance One Plc, and general economic concerns, combined to wipe out gains at the opening, traders said.
The SET Index fell 2.25 points or 0.39 percent to 567.59 by 0328 GMT. The SET 50 fell 0.24 points or 0.58 percent to 41.04. Turnover was 218 million baht

"I think there were locals buying early on interest rates cuts ideas and government measures, but it looks like it will be quiet today ahead of Finance One's invitation to analysts to meet this afternoon," said a senior trader at Dynamic Eastern.
The ailing finance firm's merger to Thai Danu Bank Plc, a potential blueprint for others to help bolster the ailing Thai finance industry, fell apart last week.
The firm will brief analysts later this afternoon ahead of a resumption in trading of its suspended shares on Friday, an event widely expected to drag the market down.
There remain underlying concerns surrounding the general economic outlook and how long the central bank can maintain foreign exchange restrictions without hampering the economy, analysts said.
Shares of property firm Land and House Plc fell 16 baht to 29.50 as the stock went ex-rights, traders said.
Leading bank stocks were largely flat. Petrochemicals firm Aromatics Plc added to Tuesday's gains, rising a further 0.30 baht to 8.40, while TelecomAsia Plc added 0.50 baht to 29.00.
